_metadata.purpose: x01 single revision round: hints the independent reviewers flagged with a concrete problem

items.reviewerReason: SCARECROW as one of Oz's famous travellers; BRAIN as the thing he asks the Wizard of Oz for.
items.reviewerFix: The Scarecrow already lives in Oz, so reword to: "The Scarecrow followed the yellow brick road to ask the Wizard of Oz for a brain."

current.wordAConnection: "If I Only Had a Brain" from The Wizard of Oz
current.wordBConnection: The Scarecrow walks to Oz to ask the Wizard for a brain
current.revealExplanation: The Scarecrow went all the way to Oz just to get a brain.

items.reviewerReason: BROOM because Quidditch is played on flying broomsticks; HOGWARTS because it is the school's signature sport.
items.reviewerFix: Use U.S. spelling in the explanation: "Hogwarts' favorite sport is played on flying brooms."

current.wordAConnection: Quidditch is played flying on broomsticks
current.wordBConnection: Quidditch is the big sport at Hogwarts
current.revealExplanation: Hogwarts' favourite sport is played on flying brooms.

items.reviewerReason: EXPLORE via the explorer Marco Polo; POOL via water polo and the 'Marco... Polo!' pool game.
items.reviewerFix: Mention the pool game, the stronger pool route: "Marco Polo the explorer, and the 'Polo!' every kid shouts back in the pool."

current.wordBConnection: Water polo is played in a pool (and "Polo!" is the pool-game reply)
current.revealExplanation: Marco Polo the explorer, and water polo in the pool.

items.reviewerReason: GHOST because Casper is a cartoon ghost; FRIEND through his title 'Casper the Friendly Ghost'.
items.reviewerFix: Lead with the title that carries the FRIEND link: "Casper the Friendly Ghost just wants to make a friend."

current.revealExplanation: Casper is the ghost who just wants a friend.

items.reviewerReason: Mother: grandmother; piano: grand piano. The explanation says 'Grandma', which hides the GRAND + MOTHER compound it relies on.
items.reviewerFix: Say the compound outright, e.g. 'Your grandmother might be the one playing the grand piano.'

current.revealExplanation: Grandma might be the one playing the grand piano.

items.reviewerReason: Volcano via volcanic eruptions, soda via a shaken soda fizzing over (and the classic baking-soda volcano); the idea is sound, but the explanation mentions only the soda side.
items.reviewerFix: Rewrite the explanation to name both sides, e.g. 'Volcanoes erupt, and so does a shaken soda, or the baking-soda volcano from the school science fair.'

current.wordAConnection: Shake a bottle of soda and it erupts when opened
current.revealExplanation: Open a shaken soda and you get your own mini eruption.

items.reviewerReason: NASA via the Apollo Moon program and GREECE via Apollo the Greek god; route is excellent, though calling Apollo 'the god of the sun' leans on a later identification with Helios.
items.reviewerFix: Rewrite the explanation as "NASA named its Moon missions after Apollo, the Greek god of light, music and prophecy." so it does not rest on the debatable sun-god label.

current.wordBConnection: NASA's Apollo missions went to the Moon
current.revealExplanation: NASA named its Moon missions after Apollo, the Greek god of the sun and light.
